applicable_when: With XBLOCK=128 and block_size=128 (4 warps), each CTA processes only 128 float32 elements (512 bytes). This generates 6.78M CTAs and 3,213 waves/SM. Each warp issues a load and immediately stalls for ~11.8 cycles waiting for L1TEX with only 4 warps per block to switch to, leaving 57.94% of cycles with no eligible warp. Increasing XBLOCK to 2048 and num_warps to 16 (block_size=512) gives each CTA 16x more independent memory operations so the 16 warps can round-robin through loads while others wait, hiding the L1TEX latency. strategy_description: Plan 'streaming_eviction_policy_and_increased_num_warps_for_latency_hiding' produced a kernel that crashed on execution after 4 attempt(s). Last error: kernel timed out after 60s
applicable_when: The kernel streams 868M float32 elements (3.47 GB) through a bias-add + clamp + scale pointwise op. Two distinct cache problems compound: (1) The large in_out_ptr0 tensor is accessed once and never reused — without evict_first, it pollutes L1/L2 cache lines that could otherwise hold the bias vector (in_ptr0, 128 floats = 512 bytes). The MemoryCacheAccessPattern rule shows only 26.4/32 bytes per sector are utilized (L2 miss path), and L2 compression is 0%. (2) With only 4 warps per block (128 threads), the warp scheduler has too few warps to hide the 11.8-cycle average L1TEX latency — only 0.57 eligible warps/scheduler vs 7.2 active means 57.94% of cycles issue nothing. Increasing num_warps to 8 (256 threads/block) doubles the warp pool per scheduler, giving more warps to interleave while others wait on memory. The grid-stride while loop already handles any block size correctly. All prior crashes were inside triton.autotune's benchmark harness — this plan avoids autotune entirely.

applicable_when: The kernel is a simple pointwise op (bias-add + clamp + scale) over 868M float32 elements. With XBLOCK=128, each CTA does only 128 loads — far too little work to hide the 16.2-cycle L1TEX latency. The scheduler is starved: 66% of cycles issue nothing. All prior attempts to fix this via @triton.autotune crashed because Triton's config pruner (line 229) fails when xnumel is both hardcoded inside the kernel body AND passed as a runtime parameter. This gives each warp 8x more independent memory operations to overlap, hiding L1TEX latency without touching the autotune machinery.

applicable_when: The kernel launches 6.79M CTAs of 128 threads each, producing 3,213 waves/SM. Each CTA processes exactly 128 elements — one float32 load per thread — which is far too little work to hide the 16.2-cycle L1TEX memory latency.
